newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian forex rate not sole export instrument.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian forex rate not sole export instrument.

text.p: Indonesia's central bank governor Sudradjad Djiwandono said on Friday he was not a true believer in using exchange rate policy to boost exports.

"We are not a true believer in using exchange rate policy to make our exports competitive. The monetary sector is there to serve the real (manufacturing) sector," Djiwandono said during a two-day conference on macro-economic issues facing Asian countries.
Djiwandono said that if the real sector kept complaining of distortions, it meant the financial sector was not doing its job well.
He said the current creeping depreciation of the rupiah alone could not make exports competitive.
"It's just a supporting element, because I believe competitiveness also come from productivity and from different kind of things," he said.
He said Indonesia's monetary management had been complicated by the fact that the country was an emerging market, with funds flowing in and out and all the implications that brought.
"If you want to depreciate and there is a huge amount of funds coming in, I think the market will laugh at us if we want to depreciate the currency," he said.
Djiwandono said the central bank would use monetary instruments to guide the market, and not use them against it.
"The definitions guide and against are sometime borderless but at least this is the way we are trying to do things," he said. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 - 384-6364
